correctness.rationale: The primitive unsigned incidence-lattice kernel of an even cycle is generated by its alternating vector, so the projective toric ideal is the single binomial. The Jacobian squarefree monomial ideal decomposes as the intersection of coordinate primes killing two u and two v variables; the hypersurface is S2 and regular in codimension one and hence normal. Localizing at a point with a,b zero coordinates gives product(x_i)=product(y_j) up to units and smooth factors. Nagata localization at all x_i generates the local class group with ab height-one (x_i,y_j) primes and exactly a+b-1 independent row/column relations; the bipartite incidence presentation has no torsion. A projective point cannot have a=b=m, yielding the precise maximum at a=m,b=m-1 or reversed. Checked m=2 smooth boundary and affine-cone origin difference; own exact Smith computations for 36 a,b<=6 corroborated torsion-free rank, not universal proof.
